name: apply a keyed function to the difference of the halves and add the result to both
mechanism: each round forms the difference of the two halves, passes it through a keyed function, and adds the same output to both halves (then swaps or reshuffles); the difference is unchanged by the addition, so the step is invertible for any round function, like the XOR-into-one-half design but touching both halves

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'IDEA' in section Computer science / Cryptography:

requires: a keyed round function mixing several group operations
fails_when: weak-key classes when key words are zero
